topic.name: Recognizing Standard Maclaurin Series for Trigonometric Functions

question.text: What is the sum of the series $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}+ \dfrac{(\pi/3)^3}{3!} - \dfrac{(\pi/3)^5}{5!} + \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^n(-\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots\,?$
question.explanation:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \sin x.$

\begin{align*} \sin x &= x - \dfrac{x^3}{3!} + \dfrac{x^5}{5!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots \end{align*}

Substituting $x=-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

\begin{align*} \sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) &= \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\dfrac{(-\pi/3)^3}{3!} + \dfrac{(-\pi/3)^5}{5!} - \dfrac{(-\pi/3)^7}{7!}+\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^n(-\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots\\[5pt] -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}&= -\dfrac{\pi}{3}+ \dfrac{(\pi/3)^3}{3!} - \dfrac{(\pi/3)^5}{5!} + \dfrac{(\pi/3)^7}{7!}-\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^n(-\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots \, . \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}.$

question.text: What is the sum of the series $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}- \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^3}{3!} + \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^5}{5!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^n(2\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots\,?$
question.explanation:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \sin x.$

\begin{align*} \sin x &= x - \dfrac{x^3}{3!} + \dfrac{x^5}{5!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots \end{align*}

Substituting $x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

\begin{align*} \sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) &= \dfrac{2\pi}{3}- \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^3}{3!} + \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^5}{5!} - \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^7}{7!}+\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^n(2\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots\\[5pt] \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}&= \dfrac{2\pi}{3}- \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^3}{3!} + \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^5}{5!} - \dfrac{(2\pi/3)^7}{7!}+\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^n(2\pi/3)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots \, . \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}.$

question.text: What is the sum of the series $-\dfrac{3}{2}+ \dfrac{27}{8\cdot 3!} - \dfrac{243}{32 \cdot 5!}+\cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}(-3)^{2n+1}}{2^{2n+1}(2n+1)!}+\cdots \,?$
question.explanation:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \sin x.$

\begin{align*} \sin x &= x - \dfrac{x^3}{3!} + \dfrac{x^5}{5!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots \end{align*}

Substituting $x=-\dfrac{3}{2}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

\begin{align*} \sin\left(-\dfrac{3}2\right) &=\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)- \dfrac{(-3/2)^3}{3!} + \dfrac{(-3/2)^5}{5!}-\cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}(-3/2)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+\cdots\\[5pt] -\sin \left( \dfrac{3}{2}\right) &=-\dfrac{3}{2}+ \dfrac{3^3}{2^3\cdot 3!} - \dfrac{3^5}{2^5 \cdot 5!}+\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^{n}(-3)^{2n+1}}{2^{2n+1}(2n+1)!}+\cdots \\[5pt] -\sin \left( \dfrac{3}{2}\right) &=-\dfrac{3}{2}+ \dfrac{27}{8\cdot 3!} - \dfrac{243}{32 \cdot 5!}+\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^{n}(-3)^{2n+1}}{2^{2n+1}(2n+1)!}+\cdots \, . \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\sin \left(\dfrac{3}{2} \right).$

example.title: Recognizing Series That Are Similar to the Maclaurin Expansion for Sine

question.explanation:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \cos x. $

\begin{align*} \cos{x} =1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} -\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, x^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \end{align*}

Substituting $x=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

\begin{align*} {\cos \left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)} &=1 -\dfrac{\left(4\pi/3\right)^2}{2!}+ \dfrac{\left(4\pi/3\right)^4}{4!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, (4\pi/3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \\[5pt] -\dfrac 12 &=1 -\dfrac{\left(4\pi/3\right)^2}{2!}+ \dfrac{\left(4\pi/3\right)^4}{4!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, (4\pi/3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \, . \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the series is $-\dfrac 12.$

question.text: What is the sum of the series $1 -\dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^2}{2!}+ \dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^4}{4!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, (5\pi/3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \,? $
question.explanation:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x) = \cos{x}{:}$ \begin{align*} \cos{x} =1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} -\cdots+ \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, x^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \end{align*}

Substituting $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

\begin{align*} {\cos \left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)} &=1 -\dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^2}{2!}+ \dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^4}{4!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, (5\pi/3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \\[5pt] \dfrac {1}{2} &=1 -\dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^2}{2!}+ \dfrac{\left(5\pi/3\right)^4}{4!} - \cdots + \dfrac{(-1)^{n}\, (5\pi/3)^{2n}}{(2n)!}+\cdots \, . \end{align*}

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac {1}{2}}.$
